descriptionChirho: Adjectival/participial form describing an individual who fears or reveres God, used substantivally as 'one who fears [God/YHWH]' — denotes pious reverence rather than emotional terror.

Masculine plural construct or absolute form referring collectively to 'those who fear [God/YHWH]', with or without pronominal suffixes (him/you), designating the community of the pious or God-fearers.

Plural construct with prefixed preposition lamed and pronominal suffixes, meaning 'to/for those who fear him/you' — same reverential sense as the plain plural but in a dative/benefactive construction.
Describes a state of fear, dread, or anxiety in an individual — emotional terror or apprehension rather than religious reverence, as in 'I am afraid' or 'he was afraid'.
Used as a noun meaning 'fear' or 'reverence', functioning as an abstract nominal rather than as a participial adjective describing a person.
